issue: Is the time limit for appealing an order denying a Hyde Amendment attorney's fee motion the 60-day civil deadline or the 14-day criminal deadline?
provision: Fed. R. App. P. 4(b)(1)(A); 28 U.S.C. § 2107(b); Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(1)(B); Pub. L. No. 105-119, Title VI, § 617 (Hyde Amendment)

sides.position: Hyde Amendment orders are governed by the civil appeal deadline because the fee proceeding is an ancillary civil matter that does not implicate the defendant's liberty or punishment.
cases: United States v. Holland, 214 F.3d 523 (4th Cir. 2000)
United States v. Truesdale, 211 F.3d 898 (5th Cir. 2000)
United States v. Braunstein, 281 F.3d 982 (9th Cir. 2002)
United States v. Wade, 255 F.3d 833 (D.C. Cir. 2001)
United States v. Onamuti, 103 F.4th 1298 (7th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: Hyde Amendment orders are governed by the criminal appeal deadline because the proceeding arises in a criminal case.
cases: United States v. Robbins, 179 F.3d 1268 (10th Cir. 1999)

this_court: The Seventh Circuit adopts the civil appeal deadline, joining the majority view, and rejects the government's request to follow the Tenth Circuit.
quote: Whether Hyde Amendment orders are subject to the civil or criminal appeal deadline is both an open question in this court and the subject of a circuit split.
cite: United States v. Taiwo Onamuti, 103 F.4th 1298 (7th Cir. 2024)
